strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing a clear limitation of binary masking in MDLMs
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple scales (169M, 7B), tasks (language modeling, code generation), and metrics (MAUVE, perplexity, accuracy)
Consistent improvements: +0.568 MAUVE for 169M, +1-15% accuracy on coding tasks, competitive with or outperforming concurrent works (CADD, CANDI, Loopholing)
Efficient adaptation: achieves improvements through pretraining continuation with only 100k additional steps
Practical design: only 3 trainable parameters, 12% inference overhead, complements other efficiency techniques (ReMDM, Fast-dLLM)
Thorough ablations and analysis: iso-compute vs iso-update comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, time-dependent masking analysis
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, implementation details across model scales
Honest discussion of limitations: training overhead, inference cost, diminishing gains at high compute, and when method is most beneficial
weaknesses: Limited novelty: concurrent works (CADD, CANDI, Loopholing, dInfer) propose very similar continuous feedback mechanisms; SM differentiates mainly through practical simplicity and empirical performance
Significant training overhead: two-pass approach requires 2.2× wall-clock time (139 vs 64 hours) in iso-update setting; sequential dependency between passes limits parallelization claims
Diminishing gains at full compute budget: language modeling gains shrink to near-zero at NFE 1/1; coding accuracy often negative at high NFE, limiting practical applicability

Design choices lack theoretical justification: entropy-based confidence function seems ad-hoc, sigmoid parameterization under-motivated, no principled explanation for why top-k superposition outperforms softmax over full vocabulary
Inference overhead non-trivial for production: 12.5% slowdown from top-k computation and reduced cache efficiency; compounds with other techniques
Incomplete comparison with concurrent works: coding benchmarks not evaluated against CADD, CANDI, dInfer; different evaluation setups complicate direct comparisons
Statistical significance not tested: improvements with overlapping error bars (e.g., Table 3) lack formal significance tests despite 5-seed averaging
Missing analysis: limited exploration of alternative confidence measures, weighting functions, or task-dependent optimization; entropy surprisingly not increased despite richer feedback

strengths: Clear problem motivation and well-articulated limitations of binary masking in MDLMs
Simple, practical method requiring only 3 parameters with minimal inference overhead (12%)
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple scales (169M to 7B) and domains (language modeling, code generation, math)
Strong empirical results: MAUVE improvements up to +0.568, perplexity reductions up to -26.93, coding accuracy gains up to +15.1%
Thorough ablation studies covering training share, top-k values, alternative weighting schemes, and time-dependent masking
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithms, comprehensive appendices, hyperparameter documentation, and provided code
Demonstrates practical compatibility with other efficiency techniques (ReMDM, Fast-dLLM)
Thoughtful positioning relative to concurrent works with nuanced trade-off analysis
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification: no formal analysis of why this specific soft-masking form is optimal, and the two-pass approximation error is not analyzed
Training computational cost inadequately addressed: doubles wall-clock time (~139h vs 64h) while iso-compute comparisons may mask practical impact
Performance degradation at high compute budgets: minimal or negative gains at NFE 1/1, limiting applicability beyond low-throughput settings
Limited scope of language modeling evaluation: only OpenWebText, no other pretrained models or diverse benchmarks; 169M model is small by modern standards
Design choice justifications lacking: sigmoid-based weighting, parameter initialization, and necessity of constraints like time-sampling bounds lack rigorous justification
Entropy trade-offs under-explored: ReMDM+SM sometimes increases entropy while improving perplexity, potentially indicating less coherent text
Incremental contribution: engineering improvement rather than conceptual advance; gains concentrate in specific regime; concurrent works suggest multiple viable alternatives
Insufficient analysis of detached-parameter training approximation quality and its impact on optimization
